parsed.explanation: Combined regime is tier-1 for travellers: national passport/visa rules impose birth-sex matching, border officers may refuse applicants for sex discrepancy or doubt, and suspected misrepresentation can become permanent fraud. Facility law in this worst-rated state/province allows birth-sex restriction and arrest risk; immigration custody reports sexual abuse, forced labour, solitary, while corrections adopts conversion therapy and birth-sex placement. Care restrictions, school disclosure, and counterterrorism framing of pro-transgender groups worsen adult and minor exposure. Some lawsuits/injunctions leave uncertainty, but no documented traveller-facing protection offsets active entry, facility, custody, and care restrictions. Score reflects high probability of forced outing when documents or spaces are checked, with severe but not execution-level consequences.

entry_documents.exposure: National order bars passports/visas matching gender identity; new M/F only per assigned sex. Foreign ministry cable refuses cases with sex discrepancy or doubt, requests evidence; suspected misrepresentation may trigger permanent fraud ineligibility. Reports passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded; foreign advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; courts and civil-liberties suits challenge policy, but no documented traveller-facing entry protection or guaranteed correction/release.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-country passport mismatch is read through national binary at visa/entry checks; discrepancy can escalate from refusal to fraud finding and downstream custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced-labour programmes, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse justified by gender status. National corrections adopts conversion-therapy practices and birth-sex placement; example held in men's ward 24 hours after facility arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as reliable protection for detained trans visitors; some orders enjoined but no evidence preventing abusive custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border or facility document mismatch can lead into investigation/custody, where birth-sex placement and abuse follow.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National bar on trans access to government-funded single-sex facilities; state/province law permits restricting trans bathroom use in many state-run facilities. Other state/provinces criminalise mismatched use as trespass requiring refusal to depart; one arrest and men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some state/provinces lack mapped bans, but this jurisdiction is among worst and state-run facilities are restricted; no documented inclusive-access enforcement for travellers.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Public buildings, schools, capitol facilities and some private settings create continuous identity-mismatch exposure; refusal to leave can become arrest.

care_services.exposure: National funding/promotion ban, specialized LGBTQ services shut, proposed youth coverage restrictions, state/province bans care to minors, hospital subpoenas for minors' records; custody can discontinue hormones.
care_services.protection: No traveller-facing care guarantee; injunctions may temporarily block some orders, but current operative rules restrict access.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing continuity/emergency/minor care can be outed, delayed, denied, or have records disclosed to authorities/parents.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order treats gender identity as ideology; counterterrorism strategy prioritizes neutralization of groups described as radically pro-transgender; law-enforcement investigates schools/teachers; political platform accuses trans of preying on women; majorities support birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute and some anti-discrimination rulings exist but are not shown as protecting visitors; state/province hate-crime law excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat framing authorizes document checks, facility exclusion, custody abuse, and may embolden private refusal or confrontation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face illegal care, sports bans, parental disclosure in state schools, records subpoenas, and funding denial; guardian may be forced to expose child or travel with mismatched child documents.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. Tribal gender-nonconforming traditions exist but do not offset state/national laws; no traveler-facing shield statute.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel through schools, clinics, or government facilities can force outing of child; assisting parent may attract official suspicion.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No recent state/province trans-specific violence incident or police profiling record appears in sources; official hostility leaves open questions about refusal, harassment, or confrontational police calls.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Twenty-two state/provinces and capital ban discrimination, but not this state/province; local municipal protections in one city only for municipal employees and rental housing.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Private service refusal or street confrontation may be handled by officers applying birth-sex policies; current incident rate is uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Pending litigation and injunctions make enforcement fluid; fraud finding requires elements and waiver is limited; arrest requires refusal to depart; border discretion varies; data gaps on visitor incidents.
remedies_unknowns.protection: ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ, some blocked orders, and courts provide possible recourse, but no documented reliable visitor remedy preventing entry denial, custody harm, or care loss.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty shifts which rules bind during travel but does not reduce operative tier-1 exposure; a traveller cannot rely on future litigation during entry or custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to 0.25-C's birth-sex facility/custody exposure, but this case adds national passport/visa fraud exposure, immigration custody abuse, and minor-care denial, making consequences more severe; unlike 0.25-C, border and care exposures are broader.

Below 0.35-A: border refusal/fraud mechanism resembles the Visitor Conduct Register, but documented immigration-custody abuse, facility arrest, and care restrictions push severity above mere exclusion/humiliation, while execution/imprisonment remains not highly likely.

Well below 0.65-A: that anchor has a one-time transport stop, brief holding, effective court release, and capital safety; here border/visa policies are systematically hostile, facilities are legally restricted, and custody abuse is reported, with no reliable traveller remedy.

parsed.synthesis: A visitor whose presentation or home documents diverge can be screened at visa/entry, then exposed in government buildings, clinics, and custody. Facility refusal, document questioning, and emergency care all can escalate into a birth-sex correction process. Border fraud allegations feed detention; state-run school/health rules disclose minors; counterterrorism rhetoric authorises enforcement. Injunctions and lawsuits affect residents and future policy more than a traveller in transit, so the operative regime remains continuous tier-1 exposure without reliable remedy.
